 'Growl' in school uniforms? That's just unfair... EXO shakes KSPO Dome with a 'K-pop national anthem' (Full Story)
 By 
 Bit, Jung 
 Published 
 2026-11-09 07:01

 Photo courtesy of SM Entertainment 
 [Sportschosun | Reporter Jeong Bit] Trends may come and go, but the roots remain the backbone. As the opening notes of 'Growl' rang out over EXO in school uniforms, a thunderous roar swept through KSPO Dome. Amid K-pop's many passing trends, one name has never faded. The clearest and most steadfast embodiment of K-pop's roots was still EXO.
 EXO (Suho, Chanyeol, D.O., KAI, and Sehun) took the stage on the final day of their sixth solo concert tour encore, 'EXO PLANET #6 - EXhOrizon [dot],' on the 8th at KSPO Dome in Olympic Park, Songpa District, Seoul, and met with EXO-L, the name of their fandom.
 Held over three days starting on the 6th, the concerts sold out every show, including seats with restricted views, drawing about 33,000 people. The final show, on the 8th, was also screened live in 764 theaters across 23 regions worldwide, sharing the festive excitement with fans around the globe.
 The concert was especially meaningful as it marked the end of EXO's sixth solo concert tour, which had continued since last April. After performing 27 shows across 14 regions worldwide—from Seoul to Ho Chi Minh City, Nagoya, Taipei, Bangkok, Macau, Osaka, Jakarta, Hong Kong, Kuala Lumpur, Manila, Tokyo, Kaohsiung, and Singapore—EXO returned to Seoul to wrap up a journey of about seven months.
 After starting with a fan meeting last December, releasing their new album 'REVERXE' in January this year, and embarking on an Asia tour, EXO spent 2026 filling stages once again under the group's name. Fittingly, the encore concert featured a setlist spanning EXO's present and past.
 Photo courtesy of SM Entertainment 
 The show opened with the new song 'Crown.' A gigantic ring-shaped LED, 23 meters in diameter, and truss lighting formed an enormous crown above the stage as the five members appeared in dazzling uniforms. They followed with their signature song 'Monster' and 'Suffocate,' which was performed for the first time at this concert.
 'Suffocate' was especially striking for its three-dimensional staging, which used a stair lift on the extended stage and Kinesis lights that shifted into a chevron shape. The overwhelming scale, made possible by a massive production budget, felt like watching a work of art.
 The audience's response was as fiery as the spectacular stage. After the first three songs, the members greeted the crowd amid cheers. Suho shouted, "Today is the dot of dots," and D.O. declared, "We've finished our Asia tour, and now we're bringing it to a close in Seoul. Let's have such a blast that we change the weather."
 Photo courtesy of SM Entertainment 
 The concert moved through 'Moonlight Shadows,' '24/7,' and 'Gravity' into a section highlighting EXO's signature mature appeal. From 'Sweet Lies,' with the members' silhouettes emerging beyond a curtain through thick fog, to 'Crazy,' EXO's uniquely polished, grown-up sex appeal—honed over years—reached its peak.
 Photo courtesy of SM Entertainment 
 The concert's true strength was on full display in the hit-song medley. The songs came one after another without pause: for some, they had been part of the playlist during their school days; for others, they had drawn them into K-pop. The history EXO had built was also a record spanning an era of K-pop.
 With handheld microphones, the members performed 'Tempo,' 'Lotto,' 'Ko Ko Bop,' and 'Call Me Baby' in succession, living up to their reputation as 'K-pop Kings.' Cheers erupted whenever a familiar melody rang out, and fans helped complete the performance by singing along precisely to the lyrics and fan chants.
 Photo courtesy of SM Entertainment 
 Photo courtesy of SM Entertainment 
 The excitement flowed straight into an EDM medley. As 'Lucky One,' 'Power,' 'Don't Fight the Feeling,' and 'Run' rang out, the audience rose as one, jumping and singing along in what became a 'club time.' It was an essential part of the EXO concert experience.
 The venue, which had been buzzing with excitement, filled with emotion during the winter-song medley. As it happened, Seoul saw its first snow of the season unusually early that day. On a day marking the start of winter, nostalgic songs that could change the season's temperature took the stage.
 D.O. introduced the songs, saying, "Don't EXO's old songs bring back memories? We'll sing songs filled with so many memories for EXO, especially ones that suit chilly weather like this."
 Photo courtesy of SM Entertainment 
 Then 'Sing For You,' 'For Life,' and 'Universe' rang out, followed by 'The First Snow,' which draws renewed attention every winter. What made it especially special was having a song that returns whenever the season comes around.
 'The First Snow' has become one of EXO's signature seasonal songs, resurfacing each winter despite the many years since its release. EXO left behind a song that represents an entire season, not just a hit—a further musical legacy the group etched into K-pop.
 The lyrical mood continued with 'I'm Home,' featuring the members walking on a conveyor belt against changing backdrops, and 'Flatline,' accompanied by visuals evoking the horizon and the night sky.
 Photo courtesy of SM Entertainment 
 The time-traveling journey reached its peak at the 'finale of the main set.' When the members returned in outfits reminiscent of school uniforms and gym clothes, KSPO Dome was transported back to the heart of 2010s K-pop. EXO retraced its beginnings with 'History,' moved on to the refreshing energy of 'Love Me Right,' and finally brought out 'Growl.'
 No one needed to start it. Just a few seconds of the intro to the song that shook the Korean music scene 13 years ago united the audience filling KSPO Dome.
 A melody undimmed by time, choreography the body remembers before the mind, and a singalong that missed not a single lyric. Even 13 years later, 'Growl' remained a 'K-pop national anthem' everyone could sing together—and the clearest proof of why EXO is called one of K-pop's foundational acts.
 Photo courtesy of SM Entertainment 
 When EXO-L's cheers continued even after the main set ended, the members returned to the stage and answered with 'Paradise' and 'Tender Love.'
 Fans also staged a surprise event. In the audience, card-section messages spelled out, "A story written with our youth" and "Will you join us for the next page?" A banner was unfurled with the slogan, "In EXO's journey, a dot means another beginning."
 In response, the members looked back on the past seven months and replied with promises for the future.
 Chanyeol promised, "Seeing all your faces onstage and hearing the members' voices while performing made me deeply realize how truly happy it is to be onstage. I'll come back whenever I can, with something beyond what you expect."
 D.O. said, "I think today will stay in my memory for the rest of my life. I get so much energy from seeing the happiness in your eyes." He added, "I hope you are always happy and stay healthy."
 KAI said, "I think the 'dot' is complete only when all three days of the concert are taken together. Thank you for filling the audience so we could perform on the stage we love." He added, "EXO will prepare even harder and come back in great form."
 Sehun gave EXO-L the credit, saying, "I don't think this concert is something only we put on. If we had to divide up the shares, it would be 30% for the staff, 30% for EXO, and 40% for the fans." He also mentioned his upcoming unit debut with KAI, giving fans a surprise spoiler: "The teasers start next week. I think it's fair to say we'll absolutely crush it with our performance."
 Suho admitted, "Honestly, preparing 'EXhOrizon' and the new album wasn't easy. I'm sincerely grateful to the members who trusted one another and stayed the course." He continued, "I was so happy performing earlier that I found myself wishing this moment would stop. I was happy because it felt as if, having forgotten everything else, only we existed in this venue." He promised, "I hope we continue to have a good relationship, loving and looking out for one another. We'll come back with new music and performances as soon as we can."
 Photo courtesy of SM Entertainment 
 Though they've put down a 'dot' to mark the end, the story of EXO and EXO-L goes on. EXO's horizon (EXhOrizon), with the group steadfastly holding on to its roots amid countless trends, now stretches toward another beginning.
 Photo courtesy of SM Entertainment 
 Reporter Jeong Bit | rightlight@sportschosun.com
